question: The Nizam of Hyderabad accepted British subsidiary alliance under ________________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Wellesley**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Subsidiary Alliance** was a policy introduced by **Lord Wellesley**, who served as the Governor-General of India from **1798 to 1805**. This policy was aimed at extending British control over the Indian princely states.
 
• The main feature of this policy was that the Indian rulers had to accept British forces to be stationed within their territories and pay for their maintenance. In return, they would receive protection from external threats and internal revolts.
 
• The **Nizam of Hyderabad** was the first Indian ruler to accept the Subsidiary Alliance in **1798**. This made Hyderabad a dependent ally of the British Empire, and the Nizam ceded control over his foreign relations to the British. *Hence, the correct answer is Lord Wellesley.*
 
• The acceptance of the alliance by the Nizam marked a significant milestone in British expansionism in India, as it allowed them to establish a firm foothold in southern India. This was also a strategic move to counter threats from other powers like the French.
 
• Under the terms of the Subsidiary Alliance, the Nizam agreed to disband his existing army and rely solely on the British forces for protection. This severely limited his sovereignty and made Hyderabad a satellite state of the British Empire.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Subsidiary Alliance:**

 
 
• This was a diplomatic strategy by **Lord Wellesley** to expand British influence in India without direct annexation. It enabled the British to control the foreign policies of Indian rulers while reducing their military capabilities.
 
• Under this alliance, Indian rulers were required to station British troops in their territories and pay for their upkeep. Failure to pay would result in the cession of territory.
 
• **Example:** Apart from Hyderabad, other states like Mysore, Tanjore, and Awadh also accepted the Subsidiary Alliance.
 
 
 
• **Lord Wellesley:**
 
 
• He was the **Governor-General of India** from **1798 to 1805**. Known for his aggressive expansionist policies, he aimed to establish British supremacy in India through treaties and alliances.
 
• The Subsidiary Alliance was one of his most significant policies, which allowed the British to exercise indirect control over Indian states.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Subsidiary Alliance:**
 
 
• It increased British control and influence in India. However, it weakened the Indian rulers militarily and financially, making them dependent on the British.
 
• It paved the way for further annexations and the eventual establishment of British rule over most of India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Features of Subsidiary Alliance:**

 
 
• The Indian ruler had to disband his own army and rely on British troops for protection.
 
• The ruler had to pay for the maintenance of British troops, failing which territory would be ceded as payment.
 
• The ruler could not employ any European in his service without British approval.
 
• The ruler had to accept a British Resident in his court, who would oversee the administration and act as a representative of British interests.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The Subsidiary Alliance was part of the British strategy to counter the influence of other European powers, particularly the French, in India during the late 18th and early 19th centuries.
 
• It played a key role in the expansion of British territories and influence in India, paving the way for the establishment of the British Empire.
